references.use: Teacher cross-check of conventional light/TEM/SEM,resolution versus magnification and organisation levels;do not copy unrelated clinical examples.
Teacher cross-check of organelle functions and generalised models;mitochondria support ATP production,not manufacture food. Do not copy inaccurate alt-text wording or absolute all-cell claims.
Licensed genuine plant micrographs;Hsu, Chou, Yen and Jane (2026),Figures1and3,CC BY4.0. Original full image bytes embedded;document view frames select named panels with bars intact.

items.title: Choose an instrument for a question
items.student: Make a comparison table for conventional light microscopy,TEM andSEM:illumination,what image information is obtained,specimen preparation/living-state limits and likely resolving detail. Decide which is appropriate to observe a living cell moving,to examine internal membranes in a prepared thin section,and to examine surface form. Explain why an electron image is not automatically a natural-colour picture of a living cell. These are instrument-choice cases,no pupil vacuum/electron apparatus experiment.
items.teacher: Light uses visible light/lenses and can image living or prepared specimens depending on technique;TEM uses transmitted electrons through a prepared thin section for internal detail;SEM scans a prepared surface for surface information. Conventional school comparisons involve fixed/nonliving electron specimens and vacuum preparation,not observing living cell movement. Electron intensity is recorded as greyscale;added colours are not natural organelle colours. Better resolving power separates finer structures;larger magnification alone does not ensure it. Do not turn a general instrument comparison into an absolute claim covering every specialised research exception.

items.title: Bigger image or more resolved detail?
items.student: Hypothetical instrument specifications for reasoning only:Aresolves separations of0.2µm,Bresolves0.005µm. Two features are0.05µmapart. Which instrument could resolve them under these stated limits? If an Aimage is enlarged10times on a screen,does this create new detail? Convert0.2µmto nm. Separate calibration exercise,not a measurement of the supplied photos:a2µmscale bar prints20mmlong,a feature prints50mmlong;estimate feature length and explain why resizing both together preserves the ratio.
items.teacher: Bcouldresolve0.05µmunderstatedlimits,Acan not;digitalzoomdoesnotcreateoriginallyunresolveddetail.0.2µm=200nm.50/20×2µm=5µm. These are supplied hypothetical/calibration data,not measured capabilities of the pictured instruments or a claim that any feature in the actual images is5µm. Bar and image must scale together without aspect distortion.

items.title: Plant light evidence:an onion root tip
items.student: Observe the genuine supplied light micrograph. Draw a small evidence outline and identify at least two defensible features,then list two things this image does not resolve. Distinguish stained nuclei/chromosomes and cell boundaries from a separately resolved plasma membrane. Explain why absent visible chloroplasts in this nonphotosynthetic root sample do not mean every plant cell lacks them. Caption:onion(Allium cepa)root-tip whole mount,acetocarmine stain,brightfield. CreditShoba Shanti2013,CIL43552,PublicDomain;https://www.cellimagelibrary.org/images/43552 . Original image unchanged;no calibration bar is supplied,so do not invent a measured cell size or total printed magnification.
items.teacher: Defensible evidence includes many cell boundaries/walls and stained nuclear material;some cells show condensed chromosomes in division. A separate membrane bilayer,ER,ribosomes and mitochondrial cristae are not resolved. Root tissue is not a generalised green leaf;staining/preparation affects contrast. Accept cautious labels/uncertainty and do not require a precise mitotic-stage diagnosis. Image evidence does not show living activity or every component.

items.title: Animal light evidence:a prepared human cheek cell
items.student: Observe the selected bottom view of the genuine source composite. Identify nucleus,cytoplasmic region and cell outline where supported;record uncertainty rather than naming each grain as an organelle. Compare with CL3using specimen and method limits. Caption:prepared human(Homo sapiens)cheek squamous epithelial cell,light microscopy;the record lists brightfield/phase/DIC but this selected panel's exact contrast mode is not independently mapped. Original bottom scale bar represents15µm. CreditGraham Wright2011,CIL12594,PublicDomain;https://www.cellimagelibrary.org/images/12594 . Document crop frame selects the bottom view with its bar;original bytes preserved. No pupil cheek scraping/body-fluid sampling.
items.teacher: The nucleus,cell outline and surrounding cytoplasm can be described;contrast-dependent granularity does not justify identifying ribosomes,ER or every mitochondrion. Apparent cell boundary is not a resolved lipid bilayer. Image is not a complete controlled same-cell comparison with onion root tissue;different tissue/preparation/contrast matter. Keep the15µmbar with this panel;100×objective metadata is not a total printed-image magnification.

items.title: Plant TEM evidence:a grass leaf section
items.student: Observe the genuine panelBview. Use the source labels N(nucleus),Ch(chloroplast),V(vacuole)to make a labelled evidence sketch and describe the surrounding wall. State one function using supplied biological knowledge,not a claim that a still image directly measures it. Explain why the photo does not establish every organelle's presence/absence. Caption:Brachypodium distachyon leaf mesophyll,TEM of prepared thin section. CreditHsu, Chou, Yen and Jane (2026),Figure3B,https://doi.org/10.1186/s40529-026-00499-x ,CC BY4.0 https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Document view selects panelB;original2µmbar and labels retained;source bytes unchanged.
items.teacher: The panel supports wall,enclosed cellular section,large vacuole,nucleus and chloroplast descriptions. It does not resolve a plasma-membrane bilayer or individual ribosomes reliably at this view. Published labels are provided evidence,not a blind identification test. Leaf specialisation explains chloroplasts/large vacuole;do not infer that every plant cell has this appearance. Photo preparation is not observation of a living reaction.

items.title: Animal TEM evidence:a partial mouse cardiac section
items.student: Observe the genuine TEM and distinguish a large nucleus/nucleolus region from mitochondria with visible internal folds where supported. Compare detail with CL4without claiming the same cell was photographed twice. List at least two limits of the field of view. Caption:mouse(Mus musculus)cardiac muscle,prepared70nmsection,TEM. Full cell and nucleus are not contained in frame. CreditDee Lauzon,Sue Lancelle,Marian Rice,Mount Holyoke College2012,CIL39755,PublicDomain;https://www.cellimagelibrary.org/images/39755 . Original image and2µmbar unchanged;this is specialised cardiac tissue,not a complete generic animal cell.
items.teacher: Nuclear material/nucleolus and many mitochondria/cristae are defensible;muscle fibrils are tissue-specific. Do not label every pale circle a vacuole/lysosome or claim the complete plasma-membrane outline is shown. Mitochondria support aerobic-respiration-linked ATP production;the still section does not measure ATP or contraction. Failure to see a structure can reflect section plane,resolution,contrast or field of view,not true absence.

items.title: Function knowledge is not the same as a visual observation
items.student: Use these supplied function facts to build a structure→function→cell-benefit table:nucleus contains most cell DNA and supports gene regulation;plasma membrane selectively regulates exchange;cytoplasm provides a medium for many reactions;ribosomes synthesise proteins;roughERsupports synthesis/processing/transport of some proteins;Golgimodifies/sorts/packages products;mitochondria support ATP production in aerobic respiration. Match each to a defensible model location. Mark each entry OBSERVED IN A SPECIFIC IMAGE,KNOWN BIOLOGICAL FUNCTION orMODEL REPRESENTATION,as appropriate. Do not pretend an image of a fold directly proves a biochemical rate.
items.teacher: The categories can overlap but require separate justification:an organelle may be visually identified while its function is supplied biological knowledge. Nuclear DNA is not all cellular DNA;mitochondria/chloroplasts have their own. Cytoplasm is not synonymous with the nucleus or every intracellular space. Protein-processing organelles are not all resolvable in every selected micrograph. Accept accurate alternative descriptions at this level;do not say mitochondria make food/create energy or that organelles independently form a complete living organism.

items.title: Compare generalised models without erasing real exceptions
items.student: Draw two explicitly labelled generalised models:a photosynthetic plant cell and a nucleated animal cell. Add the shared structures/functions from CL7and these plant features:cell wall for support/protection,chloroplasts for photosynthesis,large sap vacuole/tonoplast system contributing storage and turgor. Use CL5/CL6as limited evidence rather than pretending each diagram is a traced complete cell. Compare wall with plasma membrane;explain why CL3root tissue need not show chloroplasts and why selected model features are not universal in every specialised cell.
items.teacher: Plant membrane lies inside the wall;the wall is not the selective plasma membrane. Chloroplasts convert light energy into chemical products during photosynthesis,not create energy;plants also contain mitochondria and respire. The tonoplast bounds the plant vacuole;water/turgor and wall together support cells. Both models can include nucleus,cytoplasm,membrane,mitochondria,ribosomes,ER/Golgi. Many plant cells lack chloroplasts;some specialised animal cells lack a nucleus. Animal cells may have small vesicles/vacuolar compartments;do not claim they contain no vacuoles under any definition.

items.title: Make the levels-of-organisation links explicit
items.student: Construct two concept maps with labelled relationships:mouse cardiac muscle cell→cardiac muscle tissue→heart→circulatory system→mouse;onion root cell→root tissue→root→root system→onion plant. State how a tissue differs from an organ and why organelles are parts of cells,not tissues. Add the case'a unicellular organism consists of one cell':must it have tissues and organs? Explain a specific reason cells are basic units in these examples without claiming the fixed micrographs demonstrate living processes.
items.teacher: Tissues are organised groups of cells with related functions;organs contain interacting tissues;organ systems coordinate organs;an organism is the whole living entity. Organelle→cell is a part-whole relation,not a tissue stage. The onion example allows a specified root tissue such as meristematic tissue where applicable;do not claim all root cells are identical. A unicellular organism can carry out life processes as one cell and has no required tissue/organ hierarchy. A fixed image supports structural evidence,not a live function demonstration.

items.title: Construct two models and show what they cannot do
items.student: Using clean reused card,paper,string,tape or safe modelling material,construct a relief/3Dgeneralised plant model and a nucleated animal model with labelled compartments and a function key. Base features on CL7–CL8and state which selected micrographs support which parts. Record each learner's actual contribution and at least three limits:scale,colour,section/3Dgeometry,organelle positions or lack of living activity. Revise a model after a peer's evidence-based criticism. Drawings/plans alone must be marked NOT CONSTRUCTED.
items.teacher: Teacher provides safe precut pieces/blunt scissors,no food,body samples,sharp wire,glass,hot glue or unapproved materials. Observe actual making and explanation,not infer it from a group photo. Models need wall outside membrane in plant,organelles in plausible compartments,and accurate function labels;no requirement for fixed universal organelle positions or natural colours. Record unobserved contributions honestly;sort/reuse scraps. A model cannot perform respiration/photosynthesis or establish life by appearance.

items.title: Find,save and credit a checked cell claim
items.student: With an approved device,search a teacher-selected primary repository/source for one plant/animal cell structure as viewed by electron microscopy. Approved starting records:https://www.cellimagelibrary.org/images/39755 andhttps://doi.org/10.1186/s40529-026-00499-x . Record actual search/retrieval steps,title,organism/tissue,method,one structure claim,URL/date,licence/credit and a saved short original evidence panel. Share it with a partner and revise if metadata does not support your claim. Do not enter personal data or create accounts. If using the supplied offline packet only,label actual online search/retrieval NOT OBSERVED rather than inventing it.
items.teacher: Teacher provides approved access and permitted save/share method. Observe named actual search/retrieval/save/explanation actions;print/offline alternatives support content but do not certify an online search or digital action that did not occur. Cross-check original caption and licence,not a search thumbnail alone;credit even public-domain images. Preserve bars/aspect and distinguish TEMfromlightpanels in mixed figures. No unrelated downloads or clinical/personal-health material is needed.

items.title: Audit an overconfident cell poster
items.student: Audit these claims:Azooming a blurred image creates new resolved organelles;Bno chloroplast is visible in the onion root image,so it is not plant tissue;Callanimal cells have exactly the model's shape and nucleus;Dthe mouse TEMshows a whole generic cell;Eevery structure's function was directly observed in a still micrograph;Fa one-celled organism must have tissues. Repair each with evidence/limits. Review your actual constructed-model/source log separately from written explanations. Give one supported benefit of understanding cells as basic units of organisms.
items.teacher: All six claims overreach. Resolution is not digital zoom;root tissue need not be photosynthetic;specialisation includes shape/nucleus exceptions;mouse field is partial cardiac tissue;biochemical functions are supplied biological knowledge rather than directly measured by a still image;unicellular organisms have no required tissues/organs. Use specific image/caption evidence and honest model/digital action records. A reasoned benefit is evidence of appreciation in this task,not proof of a lasting attitude change.

items.title: Independent plant TEM evidence
items.student: Final-only genuine view,not released in teaching. Caption:Arabidopsis thaliana root meristem,TEM prepared thin section,sourceFigure1B. Source labelNidentifies nuclear material and the original1µmbar is retained. It is root tissue,not a green leaf. CreditHsu, Chou, Yen and Jane (2026),Figure1B,https://doi.org/10.1186/s40529-026-00499-x ,CC BY4.0 https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Document view selects panelBwithout editing source pixels. Use the actual image and final prompts only;do not infer a complete cell inventory from this field.
items.teacher: Defensible evidence includes walls/boundaries,enclosed cellular sections,nuclear material and pale vacuolar/vesicular regions with appropriate caution. Root tissue need not show leaf chloroplasts;absence from one section cannot classify it as animal or establish organelle absence. The photo/caption supply observations/metadata,not biochemical-rate measurements. Fresh plant image contrasts with the taught leaf image;printed source labels are openly supplied,not a blind identification exercise.

items.title: Independent animal TEM comparison
items.student: Use this genuine mouse cardiac-muscle TEMwith CL13for the separate final prompts. It repeats the taught source image but asks for independent evidence reasoning;the entire final set is not claimed to be unseen. Caption:Mus musculus,partial cardiac-muscle70nmsection,TEM,2µmbar. CreditDee Lauzon,Sue Lancelle,Marian Rice,Mount Holyoke College2012,CIL39755,PublicDomain;https://www.cellimagelibrary.org/images/39755 . Original bytes/bar unchanged. No teaching cards,models,worked answers or peer discussion during assessment.
items.teacher: Nuclear/nucleolar and mitochondrial/cristae features are supported,but fullcell/complete nucleus/membrane perimeter are not in frame. A cautious unavailable/not-resolved label is valid when justified. Compare like-for-like claims without treating different tissues/preparations as a controlled same-cell experiment. Written interpretation does not certify physical model construction or online research actions.
